title: Virtuosity
hook: Doing common things uncommonly well. The hardest skill in CrossFit isn't the muscle-up.
reframe: Virtuosity isn't advanced. It's what separates gyms that produce results from gyms that produce activity.
mechanism: Perfect mechanics at light loads transfer to perfect mechanics under fatigue. The reverse is never true.

title: The CrossFit Template
hook: Random is not a program. Constantly varied is not random.
reframe: Most people confuse chaos for variety. Variance has a structure — it just doesn't look like Monday = chest day.
mechanism: Randomizing stimulus prevents your body from adapting to the program. Every adaptation is temporary unless the challenge keeps changing.

title: The Aerobic Paradox
hook: The fitter you are, the harder Fran feels. That's not a bug. That's the point.
reframe: Most people train to feel comfortable. We train to access higher intensities — which means the ceiling keeps moving.
mechanism: A better aerobic engine allows you to sustain higher work rates, which means your body is doing more work at the same perceived effort — not less.

title: Human Power Output
hook: Fitness is measurable. Not a feeling. Not a vibe. Work divided by time.
reframe: Every gym talks about results. We can actually show you the number — and whether it went up.
mechanism: Power output (force × distance ÷ time) is the only objective measure of fitness. Heart rate and perceived effort measure strain, not output.

title: Dissecting the Hierarchy of the Hopper
hook: The best preparation for the unknown is to be competent at everything.
reframe: Specializing in one thing is a liability disguised as a strength. Life doesn't program for your strengths.
mechanism: The hopper model tests fitness by random selection across all modal domains. If you can't be tested without preparation, your fitness has a bias.

title: Scaling CrossFit Workouts
hook: Scaling is not cheating. Rx is not the goal.
reframe: The goal is the stimulus — not the load. A 95# Fran that takes 12 minutes missed the point. A 45# Fran that takes 3:30 hit it.
mechanism: Intensity drives adaptation. Scaling preserves the intended stimulus when load or skill would reduce intensity below the threshold that triggers change.

title: VO2 Max is Not the Gold Standard
hook: VO2 max can't be trained much. That's why it was never the point.
reframe: Exercise science spent decades chasing a metric that's mostly genetic. Meanwhile, CrossFit was training the things that actually move.
mechanism: VO2 max plateaus after initial adaptation. Power output, work capacity across modal domains, and resilience under fatigue continue to improve for years.

title: CrossFit Adaptations
hook: Ten things happen in your body when you start CrossFit. Most people only know one.
reframe: People join for weight loss. They stay because of what else changed — strength, sleep, insulin sensitivity, pain tolerance, mood.
mechanism: CrossFit training drives simultaneous adaptations across cardiovascular, muscular, hormonal, and neurological systems — not one at a time.

title: Goals
hook: We're not training you to compete. We're training you to live.
reframe: Elite performance is a narrow target. Lifelong health is a wide one. OTL coaches for the wide one — with the precision of the narrow.
mechanism: Training for longevity and training for performance use the same methods — the difference is the load, the volume, and who it's for.

title: The Log
hook: If you don't write it down, it didn't happen.
reframe: Tracking your work isn't obsessive. It's the only way to know if you're actually getting better — not just feeling like you are.
mechanism: Without logged benchmarks, you're training by feel. Feel lies. Numbers show trend — and trend is the only honest feedback a program can give.

title: Aging and CrossFit
hook: Muscle mass is the pension you fund in your 40s and spend in your 70s.
reframe: Aging is not decline. Sedentary aging is decline. These are different problems with different solutions.
mechanism: Resistance training and high-intensity work in midlife preserve fast-twitch fiber mass, bone density, and insulin sensitivity — the three metrics that determine quality of life at 75.

title: Coaching
hook: The best coaches aren't the most knowledgeable. They're the best observers.
reframe: Knowing the movement is the entrance exam. Seeing what a specific person needs, in this rep, in this class — that's the job.
mechanism: Effective coaching requires pattern recognition, not just technique recall. The coach who sees the athlete, not the movement, produces faster results.

title: It's Not About the WOD
hook: People don't stay for the workouts. They stay for who they become.
reframe: If the workout was the product, any app would replace us. The workout is the excuse to show up. Community is why people don't leave.
mechanism: Social accountability and identity-based belonging are the strongest predictors of long-term exercise adherence — not program quality alone.

title: A Deft Dose of Volume
hook: More is not harder. More is often just longer.
reframe: The gym that runs you into the ground every session is not working harder — it's just accumulating fatigue without accumulating fitness.
mechanism: Effective volume is the minimum dose that drives adaptation. Beyond that threshold, you're recovering from the workout rather than adapting to it.

title: CrossFit and Diabetes
hook: Exercise is medicine. CrossFit's prescription is specific.
reframe: The gym is often the last intervention when it should be the first. We've watched people change labs — not just aesthetics.
mechanism: High-intensity training improves insulin sensitivity more effectively than moderate-intensity continuous exercise. Muscle contraction drives glucose uptake independent of insulin.

title: The Mental Game
hook: You quit in your head before you quit with your body. Always.
reframe: Mental toughness is not personality — it's a skill. And like all skills, it transfers.
mechanism: Training under high-intensity discomfort builds a gap between stimulus and response. That gap — learning to act through discomfort — is the thing that changes behavior outside the gym.

title: Benchmark Workouts
hook: Fran is not a workout. Fran is a mirror.
reframe: We name our workouts because they're repeatable tests — not experiences you run once and forget. A benchmark you never retest is just a story.
mechanism: Named benchmarks create longitudinal data points. The only valid comparison in CrossFit is you vs. you, six months apart — same test, different score.

title: The Three Metabolic Pathways
hook: Your body has three engines. Most training only uses one.
reframe: Cardio vs. weights is a false choice invented by people who don't understand how energy works. CrossFit trains all three — because life calls all three.
mechanism: Phosphagen (0–10 sec), glycolytic (10 sec–2 min), and oxidative (2+ min) pathways all have distinct adaptation curves. Training all three creates the broad fitness that single-modal athletes lack.
